name: Double Eyelid
imageAlt: Illustrative photograph: a woman with her hands framing her face, looking at the camera
summary: A procedure to create or refine an upper-eyelid crease, assessed individually.
leadAnswer: Double-eyelid treatment is a surgical procedure that creates or refines an upper-eyelid crease, using either a suture (embedding) method or an incisional method. Eyelid anatomy decides which method applies, and whether either does, so the eyelid is examined in person before anything is arranged.

Many people return to everyday activities within around ten to fourteen days. The eyelids continue to settle over the following weeks to months, so the early crease is not the final one.

steps.label: Design
steps.body: The doctor marks the intended crease height and shape with you, checking symmetry with your eyes open and closed.

steps.label: Anaesthesia
steps.body: Local anaesthetic is given to the eyelid area. You stay awake throughout — the area is numbed, not sedated.

steps.label: The procedure begins
steps.body: The doctor works along the marked line using the suture or incisional method agreed at your consultation, addressing excess fat if needed.

steps.label: Suturing
steps.body: Fine sutures form and secure the crease. How many are placed, and where, depends on the method used.

steps.label: Healing and review
steps.body: Swelling and bruising are expected in the first days, and a review appointment checks how the eyelid is healing. How the crease settles differs between individuals.

sections.heading: What is double-eyelid treatment?
body: A double eyelid is the crease across the upper eyelid. Many people of Asian descent naturally have a single eyelid without one. Double-eyelid treatment is a surgical procedure that forms or adjusts that crease.
list: Creating an upper-eyelid crease where there is a single eyelid
Refining a faint or uneven crease
Reducing the effort of achieving a crease with eye make-up

sections.heading: Methods: suture and incisional
body: There are two broad approaches. The suture (embedding) method uses small access points through which fine sutures are placed to form the crease, without a continuous incision. The incisional method uses an incision along the intended crease line and is sometimes considered where there is excess skin or fat, or where a suture approach is less suitable.
The suture method generally involves shorter swelling; the incisional method tends to hold longer.

faqs.q: How long do the results last?
faqs.a: It depends on the method and how your eyelids heal. The incisional approach tends to hold longer than the suture approach, but no specific duration can be promised.

faqs.q: Am I suitable for double-eyelid treatment?
faqs.a: It depends on your eyelid anatomy and health. Dry-eye disease, uncontrolled high blood pressure, circulation disorders, thyroid disease, diabetes, glaucoma and heart disease can rule it out, so bring your full medical history.
The eyelid is numbed with local anaesthetic, and you stay awake. Tightness, swelling or tenderness while healing is common and typically settles.

faqs.q: How long is the recovery after double eyelid surgery?
faqs.a: Many people return to everyday activities within around ten to fourteen days, generally sooner with the suture method. The eyelids keep settling for weeks to months after that, so the early crease is not the final one.

faqs.q: What is the difference between the suture and incisional methods?
faqs.a: The suture method forms the crease with fine sutures through small access points, without a continuous incision, and generally means shorter swelling. The incisional method uses an incision along the crease line and tends to hold longer. Your eyelid anatomy decides which applies, if either.
